## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Fix the retry cap before merge: `fetch_with_retry` allows and defaults to 10 attempts, which breaks the project's 5-attempt "must" rule. The same pull request raises that rule to 10 on the basis of an unsupported claim about the upstream.

## Changes
This pull request adds `fetch_with_retry` to `app/net.py`, which retries `fetch` on `OSError` up to 10 attempts with a fixed delay, and adds tests for it. It also raises the retry cap in `AGENTS.md` from 5 to 10 and adds a text fixture.

## Critical
- app/net.py:19 — correctness — Cap fetch_with_retry attempts at 5 per AGENTS.md — A default call `fetch_with_retry(url)` against a down upstream makes 10 calls, and `attempts=10` passes the `1 <= attempts <= 10` check. That breaks AGENTS.md:5: "Retry helpers under app/ must cap attempts at 5. Unbounded retries have caused outages when an upstream was down." The same diff edits that line to 10, citing only "The upstream now sheds load itself", with no supporting evidence. — When an upstream is down, every caller sends twice the load the policy allows: the outage pattern the rule exists to prevent. — Fix: Set the default and the upper bound to 5 and update `test_fetch_with_retry_default_attempt_count` and `test_fetch_with_retry_rejects_attempts_outside_range`; if the cap really must change, make that policy change separately with evidence about the upstream.

## Suggestions
- app/net.py:24 — correctness — Should permanent HTTP errors be retried? — A URL that returns HTTP 404 raises `urllib.error.HTTPError`, which is a subclass of `OSError`, so `except OSError` retries it on every attempt. With the defaults, that means 10 requests and 4.5 s of sleep before the same error is raised. — Callers wait several seconds to see non-transient client errors, and each one adds repeated load on the upstream. — Fix: Re-raise `urllib.error.HTTPError` with a 4xx status right away, and retry only connection errors and 5xx responses.
